item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find any 2024 source showing Trọng endorsing genuine multiparty competition, independent electoral institutions, or the possibility that the CPV could lose power through elections. The only counterpoint is the formal existence of elections and technically allowed independents, but every source I found says those candidates were controlled or screened by the party, which makes the “pro” case non-genuine.","evidence":[{"title":"Vietnam: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/vietnam/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Vietnam is a one-party state. Some independent candidates are technically allowed to run in legislative elections, but most are banned in practice. This is the closest evidence on the “yes” side, but it does not show real acceptance of contestable power.","question_ids":["4B.1"]},{"title":"Vietnam: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/vietnam/freedom-world/2024","summary":"National Assembly elections are tightly controlled by the CPV; technically independent candidates are vetted by the CPV; genuinely independent candidates are disqualified; the CPV controls all electoral bodies.","question_ids":["4B.1"]},{"title":"Vietnam: A Gloomy Year for Human Rights","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-01-11","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/vietnam-gloomy-year-human-rights","summary":"HRW says Vietnam broadly repressed civil and political rights, punished those challenging the CPV’s monopoly on power, and prohibited independent labor unions and human rights organizations. That is direct counterevidence to meaningful electoral contestability.","question_ids":["4B.1"]},{"title":"Vietnam: UN Review Should Call for Urgent Reform","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-04-22","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/22/vietnam-un-review-should-call-urgent-reform","summary":"HRW reports more than 160 political prisoners and arrests of people for peacefully exercising basic rights in early 2024. This shows the regime was still punishing dissenters and potential challengers rather than opening political competition.","question_ids":["4B.1"]},{"title":"Vietnam","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2025 report on 2024 events","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/vietnam","summary":"HRW says independent unions, media, and political parties remain prohibited; the CPV dominates every election; and in 2024 courts convicted at least 43 rights campaigners. This is the clearest summary of the 2024 structure: elections existed, but not as a real contest for power.","question_ids":["4B.1"]}]}
